environmentVariables.description: Tool registration strategy (the --load-mode flag overrides this). 'eager' (default): register all tools at startup. 'lazy': defer Compute and Object Storage behind 'ionos_load_compute_tools' / 'ionos_load_objectstorage_tools' sentinel tools (requires MCP client support for notifications/tools/list_changed). 'dynamic' (alias 'search'): expose only the ionos_search_tools / ionos_describe_tools / ionos_call_tool meta-tools and browse the full catalog through them — for clients with hard tool caps and no tool search of their own (Cursor, Windsurf).
environmentVariables.name: IONOS_MCP_LOAD_MODE

environmentVariables.description: Opt in to write operations. Unset (default) leaves the server read-only: only list_/get_/head_ tools are registered. 'write' additionally registers create_/update_ tools and the non-disruptive actions (start_, resume_, attach_, assign_); 'destructive' also registers delete_ and the disruptive actions (stop_, reboot_, suspend_, upgrade_, restore_, detach_, recreate_, import_) and implies 'write'. Comma-separated, case-insensitive, hierarchical; unrecognised values stay read-only. WARNING: enabling this lets an AI model provision, modify and delete billable resources in a live IONOS CLOUD account. Every create and delete requires a two-phase confirmation, but that cannot stop a client configured to approve tool calls automatically. Leave unset unless writes are needed.
environmentVariables.name: IONOS_MCP_TOOL_SCOPE

environmentVariables.name: IRIS_LLM_JUDGE_MAX_COST_USD_PER_EVAL

environmentVariables.description: A priced judge model; answers_the_ask then asks it on every evaluation with input, sending that input and output to the model's provider, and gates on its verdict (off by default)
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_RELEVANCE_JUDGE_MODEL

environmentVariables.description: What every judge call together may spend per UTC day, per tenant, in USD (default 1): the relevance judge, evaluate_with_llm_judge and verify_citations. Past it no judge call is made
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_LLM_JUDGE_DAILY_BUDGET_USD

environmentVariables.description: The name of IRIS_LLM_JUDGE_DAILY_BUDGET_USD before 0.21.0. Read when the new name is unset, and it then limits every judge call
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_RELEVANCE_JUDGE_DAILY_BUDGET_USD

environmentVariables.description: Relevance judge calls one request may make (default 20)
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_RELEVANCE_JUDGE_MAX_CALLS_PER_REQUEST

environmentVariables.description: on (default) replaces the PII and credentials no_pii flags before the relevance judge sends input and output to its provider; off sends them as they are
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_RELEVANCE_JUDGE_REDACT

environmentVariables.description: Let verify_citations fetch URLs (off by default); a tool argument can turn it off for a call, never on

environmentVariables.description: Start the dashboard alongside the server (same as --dashboard)

environmentVariables.description: Dashboard port (default 6920); IRIS_PORT is the MCP HTTP transport port (default 3000)
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_DASHBOARD_PORT

environmentVariables.description: MCP HTTP transport port (default 3000); only used with --transport http

environmentVariables.description: OTLP/HTTP collector URL; when set, every stored trace is also exported as OpenTelemetry spans (best-effort, asynchronous)
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_OTEL_ENDPOINT

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated domain allowlist for verify_citations fetches (only consulted when IRIS_CITATION_ALLOW_FETCH is on); a tool argument can narrow it, never add to it
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_CITATION_DOMAINS

environmentVariables.description: The most one verify_citations call may spend on judge calls, in USD (default 1); max_cost_usd_total can lower it, never raise it
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_CITATION_MAX_COST_USD_TOTAL

environmentVariables.description: Transport: stdio (default) or http; same as --transport

environmentVariables.description: Bind host for the HTTP transport (default 127.0.0.1); only used with --transport http

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated Origin allowlist for the HTTP transport and dashboard CORS (default http://localhost:*)
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS

environmentVariables.description: The most array elements and object keys one input may hold before it is validated (default 100000): a tool call's arguments, and a dashboard or OTLP JSON request body. A tool call over it gets an error result; a body, 413. OTLP protobuf has its own ceiling, one element per 5 bytes of the request size limit
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_MAX_INPUT_ELEMENTS

environmentVariables.description: The name of IRIS_MAX_INPUT_ELEMENTS before 0.21.0, read when the new name is unset
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_MAX_TOOL_INPUT_ELEMENTS

environmentVariables.description: Bind host for the dashboard (default 127.0.0.1); same as --dashboard-host
environmentVariables.name: IRIS_DASHBOARD_HOST

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated key=value headers sent with every OTLP export (for example an auth token for your collector)

environmentVariables.description: service.name resource attribute on exported spans (default iris-eval)

environmentVariables.description: Timeout in milliseconds for each OTLP export request

environmentVariables.description: The receiver of the webhook that fires on a moment (docs/webhooks.md); merged over notify.webhook in config.json

environmentVariables.name: EARVELDAJA_DISABLE_PROGRESS

environmentVariables.description: Connection a freshly started server activates when several are configured: an index or the exact connection name shown by list_connections. Default: index 0. An unknown value fails startup instead of silently using index 0.
environmentVariables.name: EARVELDAJA_DEFAULT_CONNECTION

environmentVariables.description: Absolute path to a regular file. When set, everything the server writes to stderr is also appended to this file (mode 0o600). Off by default. Cross-platform. Useful when the MCP host swallows stderr. Pipes, devices, sockets, /dev/stdout, and /proc/self/fd/* are refused so the tee cannot corrupt the MCP stdio transport.
environmentVariables.name: EARVELDAJA_LOG_FILE
